value: No licence or copyright statement printed; ASEAN-Japan Steel Initiative public technology reference intended for public and private sectors; numbers extracted as facts only.

ASEAN-Japan Steel Initiative (AJSI) (2016). Technologies Customized List & Technologies One-by-One Sheets, Version 2.0: Energy Saving, Environmental Protection and Recycling for ASEAN Steel Industry. September 2016. 74 pp. (Japanese side coordinated by the Japan Iron and Steel Federation; publisher not printed.)

Locator: printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 2). Publisher not printed; the document is issued under the ASEAN-Japan Steel Initiative (JISF is the Japanese coordinator, referenced only via the SOACT link), so the id uses ajsi. All effects are calculated for an ASSUMED model ASEAN mini-mill (100% scrap, 500,000 t/yr, 80 t EAF at 430 kWh/t, walking-beam reheating furnace at 1,450 MJ/t, NG LHV 44 MJ/m3N); these baseline values are loaded as conventional EAF and reheating furnace examples. Main file: model EAF and reheating furnace, A-1 and A-2 scrap-preheating EAFs (SEC = 430 minus printed saving; capex = assumed investment / 500,000 t/yr, incremental, Japanese cost), D-6 induction billet heater for direct rolling, and the by-product-gas GTCC efficiency (Annex 2). _measures: all 33-technology table rows with a number (savings, Japan investment, payback) and the 11 blast-furnace-route technologies of Annex 2 (kg CO2/t and GJ/t, reprinted from SOACT/NEDO 2008). Not loaded: Annex 1 full list (136 technologies, values reprinted from EPA-BACT 2010, SOACT 2010, NEDO 2008, already held via other extractions), Annex 3 financing, Annex 4 country effects, environmental-only items B-1..B-5, C-1, C-2 (no energy numbers). Traps: price year not stated (2016 assumed); 'Electricity saving' of D-6 is negative (-40 kWh/t = increase); payback 'in Japan'; investments are 'in Japan' and may differ in ASEAN.
